sections.h2: Where is Colorado Springs, and why does it matter for property tax?
sections.html:
Colorado Springs is the county seat of El Paso County, in east-central Colorado near the base of Pikes Peak, about 70 miles south of Denver. Wikipedia lists its elevation at roughly 6,011 feet and its area at 195.761 square miles, which makes it the largest municipality in Colorado by area.

The size has a tax effect. A house on the western edge near the foothills and one in a newer subdivision on the far east side can sit in different school, fire and metro districts, so their bills differ even when the values match. The Colorado Springs Company laid out the town in 1871, and it was incorporated on June 19, 1886, so the housing stock ranges from historic districts to recent construction.

sections.h2: What does the City of Colorado Springs charge in property tax?
sections.html:
The city's own levy for tax year 2025, billed in 2026, is 3.009 mills, down 0.545 from 3.554 the year before. That figure comes from the El Paso County Treasurer's published mill levy table, and it is only one line on a bill.

The Treasurer explains that one mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, and that the total comes from applying all levies from counties, cities, school districts and special districts. The city does not mail its own bill, because El Paso County bills and collects for every taxing body in the county.

sections.h2: Which school district levies apply around Colorado Springs?
sections.html:
School levies are the largest single piece of most bills, and they vary by district. The Treasurer's table lists the following for tax year 2025.

School districtMills, tax year 2025
Colorado Springs School District 1137.695
Harrison School District 239.989
Academy School District 2045.459
El Paso County School District 4945.649
Widefield School District 357.682
Fountain-Fort Carson School District 829.765

The state's Division of Property Taxation says school districts calculate their rates separately from local governments, and its 2026 residential assessment rate for schools is 7.05%. Your tax statement shows which district applies to the parcel, so check that line before comparing two houses.

sections.h2: What other districts can appear on a Colorado Springs bill?
sections.html:
Fire, improvement and metro districts can add to the total. The Treasurer's table lists many, and the examples below show the range.

  • Broadmoor Fire Protection District: 4.5 mills for tax year 2025.
  • Black Forest Fire Protection District: 15.65 mills.
  • Old Colorado City Security and Maintenance District: 13.416 mills.
  • Banning Lewis Ranch Metro District No. 2: 46.469 mills, with other districts in that area at different levels.

Metro districts finance roads, water and parks in newer subdivisions, and the levies listed for them run far higher than for city or county services. A seller in a metro district should expect a buyer's lender and title company to ask about it.

sections.h2: What are the Colorado Springs property tax dates for the year?
sections.html:
The El Paso County Treasurer publishes a full calendar, and the dates below come from it. Weekend or holiday due dates roll to the next business day.

DateWhat happens
January 10Assessor certifies the prior year's tax warrant to the Treasurer
January 28Tax statements must be mailed
Last day of FebruaryFirst-half payment due
March 31Senior tax deferral applications due to the State Treasurer
April 30Full-year payment due
June 15Second-half payment due; unpaid taxes then become delinquent
JulyDelinquent notices are mailed and interest applies
SeptemberDelinquent real estate taxes are advertised for public auction
After September 30Cash or certified funds only
OctoberDelinquent real estate taxes are sold at public auction

For 2026 the Treasurer's notice sets registration for September 30, 2026 and the sale for October 28, 2026, held electronically through RealAuction. Interest on late payments is 1% per month with no grace period and no partial payments.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Colorado Springs property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online, in person or by mail, and the method affects timing. The Treasurer lists these options.

  • Online: current-year taxes through the Property Tax Search and Payment Portal by credit, debit or ACH.
  • In person: by credit or debit card at the office, with card processing fees passed to the cardholder.
  • Mail: a USPS postmark on or before the due date counts for current-year payments. On-site postage metering does not.
  • Fixed income: owners can enroll in monthly payments through EscrowTaxes.
  • Tax liens and redemptions: cash, cashier's check or money order, and postmarks are not accepted.

Card payments for current-year taxes stop being accepted after September 30. If a mortgage company pays the bill, the Treasurer advises owners to confirm with the lender whether taxes are held in escrow, because statements go to the owner of record rather than the lender.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Colorado Springs assessment?
sections.html:
You contact the El Paso County Assessor first, then the Board of Equalization. The Assessor's office is at 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2300, phone (719) 520-6600, and it encourages an informal call before a formal appeal.

For 2026 the Clerk to the Board of Equalization, at the same address in Suite 2201, set a real property protest date of July 15, with hearings running July 6 through August 5 by Teams. Each side gets 10 minutes, the owner must prove the value, and the written decision comes within five business days. The Board's number is (719) 520-6430.

  • Evidence must rest on market data from January 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 for the 2025 and 2026 values.
  • An appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals, district court or arbitration must be filed within 30 days of the decision.
  • The district court option goes through the Fourth Judicial District Court at 270 S. Tejon Street.

Binding arbitration, available through the county, is final and cannot be reviewed.

sections.h2: Is there a senior property tax break in El Paso County?
sections.html:
Yes, if state funding is available. The El Paso County Assessor says the exemption removes up to 50% of the first $200,000 of a primary residence's value, and that the General Assembly reinstated funding for tax year 2026, payable in 2027.

A first-time applicant must be 65 or older on January 1, and must have been owner of record and lived in the house for at least 10 consecutive years. Surviving spouses have a separate path. The page gives a July 15 deadline for tax year 2026 but also says the window has closed, so call (719) 520-6600 to confirm what applies to your case. The Division of Property Taxation also describes a senior deferral, which becomes repayable when the home is sold.

sections.h2: How do wildfire and weather affect Colorado Springs sellers?
sections.html:
The city sits at the foot of the Rockies, and its largest recent wildfire reached homes inside the city. Wikipedia reports that the Waldo Canyon Fire began June 23, 2012 about 4 miles northwest of the city, destroyed 347 homes, killed two people within the city and forced about 32,000 residents to evacuate.

The climate is semi-arid, with about 243 sunny days a year, around 16.5 inches of precipitation and about 38 inches of snow a season, with March the snowiest month. Roofs, insulation and defensible space therefore shape a buyer's view of a Colorado Springs house. The Colorado Springs Fire Department runs a Hillside Overlay and wildfire readiness program, so owners near the western hills should ask the city about requirements before work or a sale.

sections.h2: What drives the Colorado Springs housing market?
sections.html:
The economy rests mainly on the military, high technology and tourism, in that order. Wikipedia lists Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases, Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station, U.S. Space Command, Fort Carson and the Air Force Academy as military installations here.

Interstate 25 runs through the city for nearly 18 miles, and the second-largest commercial airport in Colorado, Colorado Springs Airport, has operated since 1925. Neighborhoods named by Wikipedia include Old Colorado City, Ivywild, the Old North End, Broadmoor and Banning Lewis Ranch.

Owners who must move for a new posting or a job change, or who are behind on a bill, can sell as-is. The title company pays unpaid El Paso County tax from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Colorado Springs?
faqs.a: The El Paso County Treasurer. The city sets a levy of 3.009 mills for tax year 2025, but the county mails the statement and collects for all taxing districts.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on late Colorado Springs property tax?
faqs.a: The El Paso County Treasurer says late payments accrue 1% interest per month, with no grace period. Partial payments are not allowed.

faqs.q: When does Colorado Springs sell delinquent tax liens?
faqs.a: The 2026 sale is scheduled for October 28, 2026, electronically through RealAuction, with registration opening September 30, 2026.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Colorado Springs property tax appeal?
faqs.a: Start with the El Paso County Assessor at 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2300, or the Property Record Search page. The next step is the Board of Equalization, which set a July 15, 2026 protest date for real property.

faqs.q: What happens to a Colorado Springs tax deferral when I sell?
faqs.a: Repayment is required when the property is sold or title transfers. The deferral is a loan from the state treasurer recorded as a lien, with interest accruing from May 1.
